text:
AcmeCorp (external): Hey Redwood, our streaming responses cut out intermittently after ~40-120s for on-prem customers behind our corporate gateway. Hosted calls to the same model work fine. We see partial outputs and the client reconnects producing duplicate tokens/billing spikes. Can you help?

elaine-support: Sorry you're hitting this — opened an investigation. Quick Qs: is this the Dedicated instance you have with VPC peering, or the Private on-prem package?

AcmeCorp (external): Private on-prem package, ingress through a corporate proxy (BlueProxy v3.2) then into our nginx fronting the Redwood agent. MTU on their LAN is standard 1500, the VPC on our side expects 9001 for jumbo frames.

mike-sre: That MTU mismatch stands out. Fragmentation during a long SSE chunk can cause middleboxes to drop the continuation segments. Do you have a pcap or curl reproducer we can run?

AcmeCorp (external): I captured a small trace. Attaching snippet here (redacted). They also run TLS inspection and a proxy that terminates and re-issues TLS.

sam-eng: Can you try a quick reproducer on your side and paste the command? We typically recommend:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -N \
  "https://private.example.redwood/api/v1/stream?model=red-codex"
```

We look for a continuous stream of lines like `data: {...}\n\n`. If the stream cuts, the client often reconnects and app logic replays prompts -> duplicate billing.

jess-support: From support logs I see the disconnects line up with large response chunks being emitted ~48-70s after start. On host side, kernel is sending a 16KB chunk; corp proxy's TCP MSS is 1460 leading to fragmentation. The proxy's TLS inspector reassembles but has a 65535 buffer; if reassembly stalls the inspector kills the connection after ~60s.

mike-sre: TLDR: fragmentation + TLS-inspecting proxy + a short inspection timeout = dropped SSE connections mid-payload. Two mitigation paths: (1) reduce chunk size / emit heartbeat comments to keep the proxy happy, (2) change network path/proxy config to support larger reassembly windows / longer inspection timeouts.

elaine-support: Could we ask Acme to try a quick workaround: enable smaller streaming chunking on the Dedicated/Private agent? We have a runtime flag for chunk size and keepalive interval. Sam, can you paste the config knobs?

sam-eng: Yes — on the agent config you can set: `stream.chunk_size_bytes` and `stream.keepalive_interval_ms`. Example: `stream.chunk_size_bytes=2048` and `stream.keepalive_interval_ms=20000` sends a 20s keepalive comment to prevent inspectors timing out. Also `http.tcp_nodelay=true` to reduce TCP coalescing (depends on upstream proxy honoring it).

jess-support: Also request the customer try the client option `-H "Connection: keep-alive"` and `--no-buffer` / `-N` to avoid curl buffering. For their app, adding an explicit SSE ping comment `:keepalive\n\n` every 25s fixed a similar case last month.

AcmeCorp (external): We'll try changing the agent config and add keepalive. Any server-side/billing implications?

elaine-support: The keepalive ping is a zero-byte comment event and is not billed. Duplicate token billing occurs when the client reconnects and resubmits input. Our SDKs can also attach an idempotency token to the initial request so reconnects don't reconsume the same prompt. Recommend adding `x-idempotency-key` if possible.

mike-sre: For a repro we also want: a short tcpdump of the 3-way, the TLS inspector logs (if they can get them), and the agent logs (we'll provide the exact agent log grep). If the proxy resets with RST we should see `FIN`/`RST` around the time of drop.

sam-eng: Grep command for agent logs: `sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -o cat | grep -E "STREAM|SSE|chunk|keepalive" -n --color=never | tail -200`

deploy-bot: NOTE: created ticket INF-8421 and linked customer's Dedicated/Private deployment ID. Assigned to mike-sre.

mike-sre: If customer can't change proxy config, we can push a short-term server-side mitigation on their tenant: enable `stream.chunks_fallback=true` which causes the runtime to cap chunk outputs to ~2KB and emit keepalive comments every 25s. That reduces peak TPS slightly but avoids disconnects. We need ops approval for a per-tenant setting.

elaine-support: I'll propose the per-tenant change; in the meantime please try the agent config change and the idempotency header. Also ask them to test with a direct path (bypass corporate TLS inspector) if feasible to prove the proxy is the cause.

AcmeCorp (external): Quick update — after reducing chunk_size to 2048 and enabling keepalive we saw no disconnects in 3 test runs (~10 min each). We'll keep monitoring. Thanks all. :tada:

sam-eng: Great. Follow-ups: 1) We should capture an example pcap showing fragmentation to add to KB, 2) add a help doc for `stream.chunks_fallback` and explain tradeoffs, 3) consider exposing an automatic detection: if we observe an SSE client half-close pattern we auto-enable smaller chunks for that tenant for 24h.

jess-support: Agree; adding to backlog. I'll file a doc PR with config examples and an FAQ on corporate proxies + TLS inspection.

mike-sre: Closing loop: the root cause in this case was MTU/MSS-induced fragmentation interacting poorly with TLS-inspecting corporate proxies that have short reassembly/inspection timers. Workarounds are smaller chunk sizes, periodic SSE comments (keepalives), and/or adjusting proxy reassembly timeouts.

elaine-support: Marking resolved for now; reopen if customer sees flakiness after longer soak. Thanks team. :heart:
